assumptions: The barcode channels are named by their mass ((Pd102)Di, 102Pd…), which is how they are found.
limits: An estimated cutoff comes from each barcode's own yield curve, so a barcode with few events gets a noisy one; a fit that fails gives that barcode cutoff 1 (nothing kept), as CATALYST applies it.
bio.jane/contract.question: Which barcoded sample does each event of a pooled mass cytometry acquisition belong to?

description: CATALYST single-cell debarcoding of a barcoded mass cytometry FCS file in the project, with a barcoding key (a CSV: barcode id, then one 0/1 column per barcode mass): each event's barcode from the order of its asinh-transformed barcode channels, the channels scaled per barcode by the 95th percentile of its positive values, events whose separation is below the cutoff (one for every barcode, or each barcode's own estimated from its yield curve, estCutoffs) or whose Mahalanobis distance from their barcode's population exceeds the cutoff unassigned; per-barcode yields.

_files.description: The project: record references shaped like _subject. Their records become library documents a tool names in sequences/parts/document; a trace or alignment is found by file name.

_subject.description: The record to act on: exactly one of sequence, accession (+source), sample (an id from list_samples) or file ({name, text} or {name, base64}); record_index picks one record of several.

barcode_cofactor.description: barcode intensities read as asinh(x / barcode_cofactor); CATALYST's 5.

document.description: the FCS file in the project, by name or id.

estimate_cutoffs.description: estimate each barcode's separation cutoff from its yield curve (CATALYST estCutoffs: a three-parameter log-logistic and a linear fit, weighted by their residuals) instead of sep_cutoff.

gating.description: a Gating-ML or FlowJo .wsp in the project; empty for none.

key.description: the barcoding key CSV in the project, by name or id; empty when the project holds one.

mhl_cutoff.description: the Mahalanobis distance beyond which an event is unassigned; CATALYST's 30.

sep_cutoff.description: the separation below which an event is unassigned; 0.35 is CATALYST's example.

name: debarcode_mass_cytometry

yields.description: per barcode: events assigned before and after the cutoffs, and the cutoff used (estimated or given)
